name: OrgService Dashboard Context
observations: The header selects an organization first and an optional service/role second; services are hidden until an organization is selected.
The Overview link routes / to the selected service dashboard, else the selected organization dashboard, else the global executive overview; there is no implicit default organization.
Clicking the active service clears it; clicking the active organization clears both; selecting an organization clears the service.
Dashboard drill-down list links use ?organization=<pk> for subtree scope and ?service=<pk> for exact service scope.
Incidents, problems and changes support synthetic ?status=ACTIVE; requests support synthetic ?status=OPEN, so card counts match list results.
The sidebar shows a scope badge for the most specific active context: service/role + organization, else organization type + parent path, else Global / All organizations.

When a service is selected in the header, list filter drawers pre-fill Organization with the service's own organization (TableView.context_service_organization_pk); this is display-only for lists with a service FK.
The People directory has no service FK, so a header-selected service scopes People to members of the service's organization subtree (PersonDirectoryView.resolve_filter_organization_pk).

name: OrgService
observations: Django modular-monolith service-management platform for Torres Vedras, Portugal.
Backend is Django 5.2; database is PostgreSQL 16 with ltree; tests use pytest.
Authorization is centralized in apps/common/authorization.py via can() and visible_to().
Run pytest sequentially: concurrent runs race on the shared test_orgplatform database.
Persistent knowledge lives in three places: README.md, the Obsidian vault at .opencode/obsidian/ (ADRs 001-012), and this memory graph (.opencode/memory/memory.jsonl).

name: GrantScope
observations: GrantScope (apps/access/models.py) optionally narrows a single RolePermission; no scope rows means INHERIT (membership org subtree plus ServiceAccess).
Scope types: INHERIT, ALL_SERVICES, BELOW_SERVICES (anchored on exactly one service or organization), SPECIFIC_SERVICE (requires a service), ORG_SUBTREE.
ServiceAccess rows are always intersected with GrantScope results; they can narrow but never widen access.
Scope evaluation lives in apps/common/authorization.py (_service_scope_q, _org_scope_q, membership_service_scope).
Open design question (2026-11-12): ALL_SERVICES on org-field models returns an unfiltered Q(), reaching every organization; this may contradict the access-flows-down rule (ADR-003).
Open design question (2026-11-12): SPECIFIC_SERVICE on org-field models grants the whole organization owning that service, not just the service.

name: Service Manager Role Cloning
observations: apps/access/scoping.py clones the base SERVICE_MANAGER role into one role per service (code SERVICE_MANAGER_<key> or SERVICE_MANAGER_S<pk>), each permission scoped SPECIFIC_SERVICE.
The base SERVICE_MANAGER role stays an unscoped template.
seed_rbac gives the org-wide roles (EXECUTIVE, OPERATIONS_MANAGER, OPERATOR, REQUEST_MANAGER, INCIDENT_MANAGER, PROBLEM_MANAGER, ANALYST, SUPPLIES_MANAGER) explicit ORG_SUBTREE scopes.
Scoping helpers use update_or_create so re-running seeds stays idempotent and does not cascade-delete GrantScope rows.

name: Service Path
observations: Service.path is an ltree field (labels s<pk>) with a GiST index, built in Service.save() from the parent's path; it enables BELOW_SERVICES scopes and Service.get_descendants().
Known gap (2026-11-12): migration services/0006 does not backfill path for existing rows, and Service.save() does not re-path descendants when a parent changes.

name: OrgService Seeding
observations: docker-entrypoint.sh runs migrate, seed_rbac and seed_default_data with set -e, so any seed error prevents the web container from starting (SEED_DATA=0 skips seeding).

seed_default_data gives every active SERVICE_MANAGER ServiceActor a per-service role (SERVICE_MANAGER_<KEY> from SERVICE_MANAGER_ROLE_KEYS, e.g. SERVICE_MANAGER_CEMETERIES) plus an OrganizationMembership at the service's organization.
tests/test_seed.py runs seed_rbac + seed_default_data and checks idempotency and service-manager reach.
Demo assignment: p.lopes is Service Manager of Cemitérios (Santa Maria, São Pedro e Matacães), plus Espaço Público, Infraestruturas e Edifícios and Limpeza Urbana e Espaços Verdes.

name: Service Offerings
observations: Formerly the workflows app; renamed 2026-11-12 (ADR-013). App apps/offerings, label offerings, URL prefix /service-offerings/, namespace offerings:.
Models: ServiceOffering (versioned definition), OfferingStep, OfferingTransition, OfferingExecution, OfferingTask; enums OfferingStatus, OfferingTrigger.
Permission codes are offering.view, offering.execute, offering.manage (no workflow.* codes remain).
PT UI labels: sidebar group 'Ofertas de Serviço', menu item 'Oferta de Serviço', plus 'Execuções'.
Request.offering is the optional FK to the ServiceOffering a request triggers; Service.offerings is the reverse relation.

Seeded default offerings: Waste Collection Request, Water Maintenance Request, and for Cemitérios (Matacães, created by p.lopes) 'Limpar cemitério' (MANUAL), 'Realizar um funeral', 'Realizar transladação'.
The seed chains each offering's steps linearly by order (one OfferingTransition per consecutive step pair).
ServiceOfferingType (apps/offerings) replaced requests.RequestType on 2026-11-12 (ADR-014); it classifies offerings via ServiceOffering.offering_type (many offerings per type).
Request.request_type no longer exists: a request's type is request.offering.offering_type. Request.offering is required in forms, PROTECT, and must belong to the request's service.
New request form (/requests/new/): service pre-selected from the header service context (or ?service=), offerings of that service (ACTIVE only) reloaded over HTMX via requests:offering_options.

OfferingStep.service_offering (nullable FK, PROTECT) names the offering accountable for a step; the responsible service is step.service_offering.service. Blank = the step's own offering (effective_offering / effective_service / is_delegated properties).

Seed: 'Limpar cemitério' step 'Executar limpeza' → Limpeza Urbana e Espaços Verdes / 'Limpeza de espaço público'; 'Realizar um funeral' step 'Preparar sepultura' → Espaço Público, Infraestruturas e Edifícios / 'Manutenção de espaço público'.

Offering builder (ADR-015): /service-offerings/new/ and /<pk>/edit/ (offering.manage, services from Service.objects.visible_to(user, 'offering.manage')). Lifecycle DRAFT → publish() (validates graph, deprecates previous ACTIVE of same service+name) → new_version() copies to DRAFT v+1. Published offerings are read-only.
The editor posts the plan as JSON; apps/offerings/builder.py has parse_definition, validate_graph, save_definition, definition_from_offering, preview_steps, steps_queryset, annotate_flow.

OfferingTransition.outcome is SUCCESS (next) or FAILURE (on error), unique per (offering, from_step, outcome). StepType.NOTIFY steps carry OfferingStep.message for the requester. Branches and notifications are declarative — no execution engine.

Offering editor: a step's responsible offering is chosen via a Distrito → Concelho → Freguesia cascade (forms.location_options); offerings are filtered to services in the deepest selected organization's subtree. Choices are limited to ACTIVE offerings of services visible to the user.

ServiceOffering.trigger was replaced (ADR-016) by on_request (listed in Novo Pedido) and on_schedule (recurring), at least one required (DB check constraint offering_on_request_or_schedule). Recurrence: recurrence_frequency DAILY/WEEKLY/MONTHLY/YEARLY, interval, weekdays (0=Monday), month_day, month, start (required), end; apps/offerings/recurrence.py gives summary and next dates. Schedules are declarative (no engine).
Seed: 'Limpar cemitério' is on request + monthly on day 1 from 2026-12-01.

ServiceOffering.sla_minutes = total SLA: sum of step SLAs along the normal (SUCCESS) path, error branches excluded; recomputed on save_definition (builder.specs_sla / offering_sla / refresh_offering_sla).

OfferingStep.is_external: handed to an offering of another service → step SLA is a snapshot of that offering's total SLA, no role, step_type TASK, shown with the responsible offering's ServiceOfferingType name. Same-service hand-offs keep manual SLA/role.
SLA inputs accept typed durations (apps/common/durations.parse_duration: '1d 16h 13m', '2h', '90'); duration_input/humanize_minutes format them.

Each ServiceOffering has one metrics.SLA record (SLA.offering FK, scope RESOLUTION, target_minutes = offering.sla_minutes, name '<offering> v<version>'), synced by builder.sync_offering_sla on save_definition, publish and new_version; active only while the version is ACTIVE. Listed at /metrics/slas/ (SlaListView, nav Analytics › SLAs).

name: Branch Deployment
observations: Pushes to main or dev deploy automatically via .github/workflows/deploy.yml (GitHub Actions), which reuses ci.yml via workflow_call and deploys only if lint, audit and test pass.
Each branch deploys with the GitHub Environment of the same name (main, dev), holding DEPLOY_HOST/USER/SSH_KEY/PATH/PORT secrets.
ci.yml runs on pull requests into main/dev and via workflow_call; it has no push trigger.
Deploy = SSH, checkout pushed sha, docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d --build, then health check.
docker-compose.prod.yml has no fixed project/container/image names so main and dev checkouts can share a server.
docker-entrypoint.sh always runs migrate and seed_rbac; SEED_DATA only gates seed_default_data.
Server setup/rollback documented in Obsidian Procedures/Deploying.md.
